Q: How can I update home screen icon of my Progressive Web App? A:

Sounds like in the comments above you got your answer, I just wanted to throw up something that helped me. My app is in React not Angular (and I'm a noob so I don't know if that would matter but I wanted to make note in case it did) and when I tried to have the app icon within the src (mine is in "/assets" like yours) it wasn't updating the icon with a refresh. To be very clear here, I only tried once - but the application tab in DevTools wasn't seeing my icon either. So instead I put the icon in my public folder within an images folder and when I reinstalled the app it had my icon perfect. I already had that folder to house my tab icon (forgot the technical term for that) so I didn't feel like I was adding anything that was bloating my app but that's my opinion.

Don't know if that helps, I didn't go down this rabbit hole trying to figure out why mine wasn't catching the image in the src/assets.

Q: How can I make a VBS Message Box appear in a random place? A:

@Hackoo was almost there, I used his and here is what I made out of it.

dim r
randomize
r = int(rnd*500) + 1
r2 = int(rnd*1500) + 1
Title = "Hello"
DefaultValueText = "Hello!"
message = "Type something here!"
XPos = r
YPos = r2
Text = InputBox(message,Title,DefaultValueText,XPos,YPos)

Q: demucs.api or demucs.pretrained aren't working A:

Yeah those code examples are all outdated. Demucs changed their API completely.

Easiest way in Python:

Those code examples are all for old Demucs versions. The API changed completely.

Just use the CLI in Python:

import subprocess
subprocess.run(['demucs', 'your_file.wav'])

Way easier than messing with the Python API. No duration limits either.

Q: Why does sorting reduces the time of my function? A:

Here, the main factor is not the sorting algorithm, it is the synchronization of Bash`s internal memory management.

The main culprit is how readarray interacts with the pipe and the shell`s process substitution.

When you run (seq 0 2000) the data is pushed into the pipe as fast as possible.

Bash`s readarray has to grab those lines and allocate memory for the array.

1> They slow path(without sort) :

The fist seq is extremely fast. It floods the pipe immediately.

readarray is trying to read and allocate memory for 20001 individual elements while the subshell is still hammering the pipe.

Bash often performs many small read90 syscalls. Without a buffer inn between , the shell spends more time managing the "handshake" between the producer(seq) and the consumer(readarray).

2> The fast path (With sort) :

The sort introduce a blocking buffer.

sort cannot output a single line until it has received the entire input( because the last number from seq might be the first one in the alphabetic order)

While sort is busy in its own dedicated process, readarray is sitting idle. Once sort finishes its internal buffer into the pipe in large, efficient chunks.

By the time readarray starts working, the data is already organized in the OS pipe buffer. readarray can then ingest the data in a much "cleaner" burst with fewer contest switches between the two processes.

For the 20000 small strings ,the actual CPU time used by sort(nlogn) is negligible likely just a few milliseconds.

The overhead of Process I/O and Memory Allocation in Bash is significantly higher that the time it takes for a compiled C program like sort to organize a few thousand integers.

Complexity(seq) => O(n) , Near instant.

Complexity(sort) =>O(n log n), Extremely fast.

Complexity(readarray) => O(n), slow(Shell memory management)

Q: Use argparse to define an option that takes a string consisting of any letters from a given set A:

Argparse does not have a built-in argument type that supports what you want, but it can be extended with a custom argument type to add support. For example,

from argparse import ArgumentTypeError

def my_argument_converter(arg):
    allowed = 'ARLQTNZCFXPB'
    for c in arg:
        if c not in allowed:
            raise ArgumentTypeError(f'{c} is not among "{allowed}"')

    return arg

parser.register('type', 'options type', my_argument_converter)
parser.add_argument('-o', '--options', type='options type', help='Control Options')

That will validate the argument against your string of allowed options, and store the whole string if it passes. If you prefer, it could perform additional validations, and / or it could return a different value to store in the argument namespace, such as a list of the individual options.

Q: How to upgrade MongoDB? A:

1.Import the public key used by the package management system

sudo apt-key adv --keyserver hkp://keyserver.ubuntu.com:80 --recv EA312927

2. Create a list file for MongoDB.

echo 'deb http://downloads-distro.mongodb.org/repo/ubuntu-upstart dist 10gen' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mongodb.list

3. Reload local package database. sudo apt-get update

4. stop the existing service sudo service mongodb stop

5. first migrate to 2.4 to 2.6 Install a specific release of MongoDB

sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-org=2.6.12 mongodb-org-server=2.6.12 mongodb-org-shell=2.6.12 mongodb-org-mongos=2.6.12 mongodb-org-tools=2.6.12

6.unlink the temp links remove the lock file. rm /tmp/mongodb-27017.sock

7.restart mongo service sudo service mongodb restart

8. Now finally migrate from 2.6 to 3.0 sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-org=3.0.12 mongodb-org-server=3.0.12 mongodb-org-shell=3.0.12 mongodb-org-mongos=3.0.12 mongodb-org-tools=3.0.12

restart again and voila !!!!

For more details follow the official documentation: mongo doc

Q: OpenMP in Fortran: "Segmentation fault" A:

Firstly,

CFLAGS = -O2
F90FLAGS = -O3 -pipe -fomit-frame-pointer -fopenmp

You will get better results if you add -g to both of those. And even better still if you use -fno-omit-frame-pointer.

I'm not an OpenMP expert, but roughly speaking the OpenMP architecture is to create a thread pool, and then whenever you use stuff like the pragma parallel for, packets of work corresponding to the for loop body will be handed to the thread pool to perform.

As for the stack size, there are two things that you need to consider. By default stack sizes are limited to 8 MB. You can increase the size limit for the main thread using the shell limit/ulimit commands. Thread stack size limits are set when the threads are created, and that can be controlled by the OMP_STACKSIZE environment variable. On top of that Valgrind also imposes its limit for the main thread. As your output says, you can increase that with --max-stackframe=.

You can get away with putting a lot on your main thread's stack. Don't put too much on your thread stacks.

You don't say what your 646464*100 array is made up of. If it is floating point doubles, then you will need about 520 MB of memory. I'd round that up to 600 MB to be safe.
